extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural investigators and grant applicants (PIs, research administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for preparing NIH extramural grant applications (e.g., R01s), focusing on what reviewers and NIH leaders consider important across Significance, Investigator, Innovation, Approach, and Environment. Includes policy- and culture-level expectations promoted by NIH leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: "Important problem with broad implications"; connection to public health priorities; filling a known gap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that the project addresses an important problem, has broad implications, connects to public health priorities, and fills a recognized gap in knowledge or practice. Explicitly state the importance and potential impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: Track record proportionate to career stage; independent productivity; collaborator strength for novel approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present investigators' qualifications in a way appropriate to their career stage (ESI vs established), highlight independence and productivity, and document collaborators' strengths when they are central to novel or multi-disciplinary approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Novel concepts, approaches, methodologies, tools; potential to shift research/clinical paradigm. Refinements vs. radical departures both count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what's novel about the project—whether a new concept, method, tool, or a paradigm shift—and clarify how incremental refinements or more radical departures contribute to progress. Avoid overstating incremental work as paradigm-shifting when inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategy, methodology, analyses well-reasoned; address strengths and weaknesses; manage risk through alternatives; sex as biological variable (added during her tenure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, well-reasoned experimental/analytic strategy with appropriate methods and analyses; acknowledge and address potential weaknesses and risks, including contingency plans or alternatives; explicitly consider and justify inclusion of sex as a biological variable where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional support; resources match the project; collaborative arrangements add capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document institutional support and available resources that enable project success, and describe how collaborations materially add capability or expertise. Ensure environment details are proportionate to project needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hit the five review criteria explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit rubric advice: 'Hit the five review criteria explicitly.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should explicitly organize portions of their application to address Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach, and Environment so reviewers can readily find and evaluate each criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate awareness of NIH priorities and policy changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate awareness of NIH priorities and policy changes (e.g., resubmission policy changes such as A2 elimination; emphasis on rigor/reproducibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that the application authors understand and have aligned the project with current NIH priorities and policies—referencing relevant policy changes where they affect design, resubmission strategy, or evaluation (for example, account for the A2 elimination and expectations about rigor and reproducibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Match career stage to aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Match your career stage to your aims (don't oversell, don't undersell).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame project scope, investigator responsibilities, and productivity claims in a manner appropriate to the PI's career stage. Early-stage investigators should avoid overcommitting beyond feasible independence; established investigators should show sustained leadership and productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NIH's own language (rigor, reproducibility, transparency, diversity)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Use NIH's own language (rigor, reproducibility, transparency, diversity)" — incorporate these concepts into applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt NIH-preferred terminology and explicitly address rigor, reproducibility, transparency, and diversity in relevant sections (e.g., approach, rigor and reproducibility statements, inclusion/diversity plans). Aligning language helps reviewers and program staff see how the proposal meets NIH expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show how your project advances public health
rubrics_metrics.description: Show how your project advances public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate the public health relevance and translational potential of the work—why advancing this research matters for health outcomes or policy—and connect project aims to broader health priorities when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a good citizen (service, data sharing, training)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be a good citizen — review for NIH, share data, train the next generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate commitment to community norms valued by NIH: participation in peer review, plans for data and resource sharing, and concrete evidence of mentoring/training activities. Such contributions are viewed favorably as part of an investigator's overall profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application length / formatting (R01 page limit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to NIH page limits and formatting rules (e.g., R01 research strategy page limit that has been set to 12 pages since 2010). Follow all submission instructions to avoid administrative issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission policy awareness (A2 elimination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmission policy changes (A2 elimination, etc.) noted as important context for applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan proposal and revision strategies mindful of resubmission policy changes (for example, the elimination of A2s); understand how these policies affect chances and timelines for funding and structure resubmissions or new submissions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of sex as a biological variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Sex as biological variable included as part of 'Approach' and noted as added policy attention during Rockey's tenure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, explicitly address the consideration of sex as a biological variable in study design, analysis, and interpretation; justify exclusions when appropriate per NIH guidance.
